note: PHASE 2 REPRODUCIBILITY FINDING — exp7 (Contribution 4) does not reproduce across environments. Recorded here because experiments/results/ is NOT under version control, so the original run would otherwise have been lost when exp7 was re-run. Original per-class values recovered from contribution4_figures/tab_contribution4.tex, which was generated from the original RESULTS.json (config 9fd36828240c).
what_reproduces_exactly: raw delta bytes per class — the twin_manager delta derivation is fully deterministic
what_does_not_reproduce: compressed sizes at zlib level 6, and therefore the uniform baseline, the HADC-vs-uniform saving, and the heterogeneous_selection flag

phase2_rerun.environment: Windows 11, native Python (NOT the stack host)

analysis.zlib9_output_identical: machine/conveyor/sensor HADC bytes are byte-identical across environments (1618, 1569, 1322)
analysis.consequence_1: The 4.2% headline saving is not a property of the method. It is the ratio between a zlib-9 result and a zlib-6 result, and zlib-6's output depends on the zlib build. The same code yields 6.25% here.
analysis.consequence_2: The published caveat 'all classes chose zlib-9, so there is no structural heterogeneity' is FALSE in this environment: agv selects zlib-6 and heterogeneous_selection is true. The caveat cannot be stated as a finding.
analysis.consequence_3: Contribution 4 as currently framed rests on an unpinned dependency. Either pin the zlib version and report it as part of the configuration, or reframe the contribution around a codec set whose outputs are version-stable.

action_required: Re-run exp7 on the WSL2 stack host and record python + zlib versions in provenance.
Put experiments/results/ under version control, or write every run to a timestamped directory. An unversioned results tree let a re-run silently replace a published measurement.
Do not cite the 4.2% figure or the all-zlib-9 caveat until the environment is pinned.
